final_rationale: The verdict does not change because there is no new admissible evidence. The Actor’s response is a more careful interpretation of the same record and appropriately concedes that aggregate readiness and post-launch monitoring do not cure a policy-triggered disclosure or approval requirement. That improved framing reduces overclaiming, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. On the available evidence summary, the enterprise refund workflow gap remains potentially material under the stated policy because the affected segment is tied to customer commitments and legal review is still open. Since the record still does not establish that the issue has been resolved, formally disclosed in the required way before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance, full compliance is not supported. The narrowed position is stronger than the original broad certification defense, but it is still an unresolved compliance question rather than a completed caveated-compliance showing.
remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the initial report; the Actor mainly narrowed and caveated the claim.

The policy text makes materiality turn on impact to a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the available summary still indicates a named affected segment plus an open legal review.
The record still does not show that the required pre-launch predicate has been satisfied: resolution, actual disclosure in final packet form, or approved risk acceptance.
Operational readiness evidence (aggregate pass and no severity-one rehearsal incidents) supports launch readiness but does not independently establish policy compliance.
Public governance and model-card guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not override the enterprise policy requirement.
